claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO introduces resonant phonon-scattering centers that scatter more effectively than the random disorder represented by a Debye-Callaway model.
MoNbTaW is a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed initial MoNbTaW or NbMoTaW material is a chemically disordered, single-phase alloy.
Arc melting followed by high-temperature homogenization ensures a random atomic distribution in the initial alloy.
Annealing at 0.4–0.6 of the melting temperature can induce significant SRO in the RHEA.
An annealing window exists in which significant SRO forms without long-range ordering or phase separation.
Rapid quenching preserves the annealing-induced SRO state.
SRO in MoNbTaW may involve Mo-W or Nb-Ta nearest-neighbor preferences.
SRO pair correlations create local potential-energy fluctuations distinct from the average lattice potential.
These local potential fluctuations act as resonant scatterers for mid- to high-frequency phonons.
Mass-variance and strain-field scattering dominate lattice transport in the chemically disordered alloy.
SRO creates local environments having vibrational densities of states distinct from that of the host lattice.
SRO-associated local vibrational modes resonate with propagating host-lattice phonons.
Resonant scattering reduces phonon group velocity and lifetime, lowering lattice thermal conductivity below the random-alloy value.
The SRO-containing sample will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than the disordered baseline throughout 300–1200 K.
SRO-induced suppression will be strongest from 300–800 K because phonon mean free paths are then comparable to the SRO correlation length.
Quenching from above the ordering temperature produces a baseline state with negligible SRO.
Ordering can drive a disordered alloy toward ordered, intermetallic, or multiphase states.
Long-range ordering should sharply increase thermal conductivity by reducing scattering in a periodic lattice.
